title: Make a commit without using git commit
summary: Build a commit from the bottom up with plumbing commands: hash a blob, write a tree, create a commit object, move a branch. After this, nothing about git is mysterious.
mental_model: `git commit` is four plumbing commands in a trench coat: store the file as a blob, build a tree from the index, create a commit pointing at that tree and at the current HEAD, then move the branch to the new commit.

setup.run: git commit -q -m "Initial commit, the normal way"

steps.title: Store a file as a blob
steps.why: `hash-object -w` computes the sha of the content and writes it into `.git/objects`. Note what it does NOT do: nothing is staged, nothing is committed, and the filename is not recorded anywhere. A blob is only bytes.
steps.expect: A 40-character sha, an object file on disk, and status still showing pump.py as untracked.

verify.label: the content is stored as a blob

steps.title: Put the blob into the index under a name
steps.why: `update-index --add --cacheinfo` writes an index row: mode, blob sha, path. This is where a filename first enters the picture — blobs themselves have no names.
steps.expect: pump.py now staged, with the blob sha you just created.

verify.label: the path is in the index

steps.title: Turn the index into a tree
steps.why: `write-tree` snapshots the index as a tree object — a sorted list of (mode, type, sha, name). This is the object a commit actually points at.
steps.expect: A tree containing README.md and pump.py, each with its own blob sha.

verify.label: the tree lists the new file

steps.title: Create the commit object
steps.why: `commit-tree` takes a tree, a parent and a message, and returns a new commit sha. Nothing has moved yet — the commit exists but no branch points at it, so `git log` cannot see it.

actions.run: sh -c 'git commit-tree $(git write-tree) -p HEAD -m "Add pump control, built by hand" > .git/handmade-sha'

steps.expect: A commit object with tree, parent, author and message lines — and a git log that still shows only one commit.

verify.label: …but nothing points at it yet, so log cannot see it

steps.title: Move the branch
steps.why: `update-ref` writes the sha into `refs/heads/main`. That single write is what 'making a commit' means from the branch's point of view — everything before it was creating objects.
steps.expect: Two commits in the log, a clean status, and a ref file containing the sha.

verify.label: the branch moved and the commit is now history

verify.equals: Add pump control, built by hand
verify.label: …with the message you gave commit-tree

steps.title: Prove it is a completely ordinary commit
steps.why: Every porcelain command treats it identically, because there is no difference. `git commit` is a convenience wrapper, not a special mechanism.

steps.title: The same four steps, the normal way
steps.why: Run the porcelain and compare. `add` = hash-object plus update-index. `commit` = write-tree plus commit-tree plus update-ref. That mapping is the whole of git's data layer.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Add dosing, the normal way"

verify.label: three commits: one normal, one by hand, one normal again
you built a commit with plumbing and git treats it as ordinary history

verify.contains: Add pump control, built by hand
verify.label: the hand-built commit is in the log
the hand-built commit points at a tree, like any other
fsck considers everything you built perfectly valid

pitfalls: `hash-object` without `-w` only prints the sha; it writes nothing. Easy to think you stored something when you did not.
`commit-tree` does not move any branch. A commit with no ref pointing at it is invisible to `git log` and will be garbage-collected.
The index must be correct before `write-tree`. Plumbing does not check whether the tree makes sense.
Porcelain output is for humans and may change between versions; plumbing output is stable and meant for scripts. That is the actual distinction between the two.
cheatsheet: snapshot the index as a tree
the tree a commit points at
